title: AF-8-part-1
description: Airframe exam covering aircraft inspection types and programs (preflight, 100-hour, annual, progressive, continuous, special), inspection phases and process, non-destructive testing (NDT) methods, and maintenance documentation and records, drawn from the AF-8 inspection and documentation question/answer bank.

questions.question: Checking the engine compartment for loose wires and fittings is normally done during which inspection?
questions.explanation: A visual check of the engine compartment for loose wires, fittings, and obvious discrepancies is a standard part of the routine preflight inspection before each flight.

questions.question: What type of inspection is performed on aircraft operated for flight instruction or hire, but is not itself FAA-mandated by name?
questions.explanation: Some operators voluntarily schedule interim checks, such as a 50-hour inspection, between the FAA-mandated 100-hour/annual inspections, even though it is not itself a regulatory requirement.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding sources that can initiate an aircraft inspection?
options: A. That aircrew reports cannot be used to initiate an inspection
B. That a scheduled maintenance program can initiate an inspection
C. That a discrepancy found during a walk-around can initiate an inspection
questions.explanation: Aircrew (pilot) reports of discrepancies are a legitimate and common trigger for initiating an aircraft inspection, so claiming they cannot be used is false.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the annual inspection?
options: A. It can be performed by any licensed pilot
B. It requires only an A&P certificate with no additional authorization
C. It requires both an A&P certificate and Inspection Authorization (IA) to perform
questions.explanation: An annual inspection must be conducted by a mechanic holding both an A&P certificate and an Inspection Authorization (IA), a higher level of certification than a standard A&P alone.

questions.question: What is the statement, notation, and signature made in the maintenance record after an inspection or repair called?
options: B. Approving the aircraft for return to service
questions.explanation: The maintenance record entry and signature certifying the work is complete and the aircraft is airworthy is referred to as approving the aircraft for return to service.

questions.question: Which inspection phase starts with a conformity inspection?
options: A. The return to service phase
questions.explanation: The "Look" (inspection) phase begins with a conformity check, comparing the aircraft's actual condition and configuration against its approved data.

questions.question: What type of inspection is required following an overweight landing, lightning strike, fire, or flood damage?
questions.explanation: Unusual or potentially damaging events such as overweight landings, lightning strikes, fire, or flood call for a special (unscheduled) inspection targeted at assessing that specific damage.

questions.question: The continuous airworthiness inspection program is designed primarily for what category of aircraft?
questions.explanation: Continuous airworthiness maintenance/inspection programs are typically developed for large aircraft operated under programs such as those used by air carriers, rather than simple small aircraft.

questions.question: To whom does the owner of an aircraft apply for authorization of a progressive inspection program?
options: A. The concerned FAA Flight Standards District Office (FSDO)
questions.explanation: Approval for a progressive inspection program is obtained through the FAA Flight Standards District Office (FSDO) responsible for that aircraft/operator.

questions.question: What type of inspection is required on an aircraft that may have flown through severe turbulence?
options: A. A routine preflight inspection only
questions.explanation: Flight through severe turbulence can impose unusual structural loads, warranting a special inspection to check for resulting damage before further flight.

questions.question: What is an inspection accomplished before the first flight of each day called?
questions.explanation: A preflight inspection is conducted before the first flight each day to verify the aircraft is in a condition safe for flight.

questions.question: What is a maintenance activity performed to detect any defects or malfunctions on an aircraft before they become serious called?
questions.explanation: Inspection is the proactive maintenance activity specifically aimed at finding defects or malfunctions early, before they develop into more serious problems.

questions.question: Which of the following can NOT be a cause for initiating an aircraft inspection?
options: A. A pilot report of unusual vibration
B. Flying the aircraft in rainy conditions
C. A scheduled inspection interval being reached
questions.explanation: Simply flying in rain is a normal operating condition and not, by itself, a trigger for initiating a special inspection, unlike a pilot discrepancy report or a scheduled interval.

questions.question: What term describes the general wear and tear of an aircraft during its service life?
questions.explanation: Attrition refers to the gradual wear and degradation an aircraft experiences simply through normal operational use over its service life.

questions.question: By how many hours may a 100-hour inspection be exceeded, if necessary, to fly the aircraft to a place where the inspection can be performed?
questions.explanation: Regulations allow a 100-hour inspection to be exceeded by up to 10 hours solely for the purpose of flying to a location where the inspection can be performed, with that excess time counted toward the next inspection interval.

questions.question: What is required to fly an aircraft after its annual inspection has expired, to a place where the inspection can be performed?
options: A. Nothing; it can be flown normally
B. A special flight (ferry) permit from the FAA
C. Only a logbook entry by the owner
questions.explanation: An aircraft with an expired annual inspection is not airworthy for normal flight and requires a special flight/ferry permit issued by the FAA to be legally flown to a inspection location.

questions.question: Inspection and maintenance program requirements can depend on seating capacity for which category of operation?
options: B. Air taxi and commercial operator aircraft
questions.explanation: For air taxi and commercial operations, applicable inspection program requirements can vary based on the aircraft's passenger seating capacity, as specified in the regulations governing those operations.

questions.question: Which inspection phase determines the actual condition of the aircraft and its components?
questions.explanation: The "Look" phase of inspection is where the technician visually and physically examines the aircraft and its components to assess their actual condition.

questions.question: Which type of inspection program is similar to a progressive inspection but is typically used on large turbine-powered aircraft?
questions.explanation: Continuous inspection programs break maintenance into smaller recurring tasks spread over time, similar in concept to progressive inspection, but are the structure commonly used for large turbine aircraft.

questions.question: Who is responsible for having all non-airworthy defects repaired before flying an airplane?
options: C. The aircraft owner or operator
questions.explanation: Ultimate responsibility for ensuring an aircraft is airworthy, including having known defects repaired before flight, rests with the aircraft's owner or operator.

questions.question: Which appendix of FAR Part 43 covers the minimum inspection requirements for an aircraft (the annual/100-hour inspection checklist items)?
questions.explanation: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix D specifies the scope and detail of items that must be checked during an annual or 100-hour inspection.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the relationship between annual and 100-hour inspections?
options: A. A 100-hour inspection is valid in place of an annual inspection
B. An annual inspection is valid in place of a 100-hour inspection
C. Neither can substitute for the other under any circumstance
questions.explanation: Because the annual inspection is more comprehensive (requiring IA certification), it satisfies the 100-hour inspection requirement as well, but not vice versa.

questions.question: An annual inspection completed on September 1, 2021 would remain valid until what date/time?
questions.explanation: Annual inspections are valid through the end of the 12th month following completion, specifically until midnight on the last day of that month one year later.

questions.question: Checking the inflation of tires must be done during which inspection?
questions.explanation: Tire inflation is a basic visual/physical check expected to be performed as part of the routine preflight inspection before each flight.

questions.question: What is a comprehensive and complete inspection that can be performed by a certified A&P technician with no additional requirement (such as Inspection Authorization)?
questions.explanation: Unlike the annual inspection, which requires Inspection Authorization, the 100-hour inspection can be performed and signed off by a standard certificated A&P mechanic.

questions.question: What type of inspection records the absorption of rays onto a film sensitive to X-rays?
questions.explanation: Radiographic inspection exposes film to X-rays (or gamma rays) passing through the part, with the resulting image revealing internal flaws based on differential ray absorption.

questions.question: What color indication shows a defect when a dye penetrant inspection is viewed under visible (white) light?
questions.explanation: Visible dye penetrant systems use a red dye that bleeds out of a defect and shows as a bright red indication under normal white light viewing.

questions.question: Around the hangar aircraft maintenance area, which NDT (non-destructive testing) method requires serious safety precautions?
questions.explanation: Radiographic (X-ray) inspection involves ionizing radiation, requiring strict safety precautions such as area control, shielding, and radiation monitoring, unlike the other common NDT methods.

questions.question: Which type of NDT inspection requires the use of a couplant?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic inspection uses a couplant (such as gel or water) between the transducer and the part surface to ensure efficient transmission of sound waves into the material.

questions.question: Which type of NDT inspection is well suited to detecting flaws open to the surface?
questions.explanation: Magnetic particle inspection is particularly effective at revealing surface and near-surface cracks/flaws in ferromagnetic materials, as particles accumulate at the flux leakage from a defect.

questions.question: What method is used to inspect the internal parts of an engine during an engine check without disassembly?
questions.explanation: A borescope allows a technician to visually inspect internal engine components (such as turbine blades) through small access ports, without needing to disassemble the engine.

questions.question: Which type of NDT inspection uses a magnetic field intersecting a circulating (induced) current?
questions.explanation: Eddy current inspection induces circulating electrical currents in a conductive part via a magnetic field; changes in those currents, caused by flaws, are detected by the probe.

questions.question: What color result is seen when using dye penetrant inspection under UV (black) light?
questions.explanation: Fluorescent dye penetrant systems glow a bright greenish-yellow color under ultraviolet/black light, making defect indications highly visible in a darkened area.

questions.question: Which NDT method uses high-frequency sound waves to detect internal flaws?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic inspection transmits high-frequency sound waves through a material and analyzes reflected echoes to detect internal defects such as voids or cracks.

questions.question: A "D" check is best described as what type of inspection program?
options: C. A continuous inspection (as part of a long-term scheduled maintenance program)
questions.explanation: The D check, the most extensive airline heavy maintenance check, is part of a continuous (ongoing, scheduled) inspection program structure rather than a single standalone event type.

questions.question: Which routine inspection can be performed by the copilot or pilot before flight?
questions.explanation: A walk-around inspection, a basic visual check of the aircraft exterior, is commonly performed by the pilot or copilot as part of preflight duties.

questions.question: Preflight and walk-around inspections are also commonly known as what?
questions.explanation: The routine preflight/walk-around check performed before the first flight of the day is often referred to as the daily inspection.

questions.question: Who is responsible for making the maintenance record entry after a 100-hour or annual inspection?
options: A. The aircraft owner personally, regardless of certification
C. The person approving or disapproving the aircraft for return to service
questions.explanation: The certificated individual who performed or supervised the inspection is responsible for the maintenance record entry documenting approval (or disapproval) for return to service.

questions.question: If a 100-hour inspection must be exceeded by 6 hours to reach a place where the inspection can be performed, what is the next inspection interval based on?
options: A. 100 hours from the flight that exceeded the limit
B. 106 hours from the original due time
C. 94 hours (counting back from the time the 100-hour inspection was actually due)
questions.explanation: When the 10-hour allowance is used (here, 6 of the 10 hours), the next 100-hour interval is calculated from the time the inspection was originally due, resulting in a shorter interval (100 minus the 6 hours used, i.e., 94 hours) until the next inspection is due.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the overall airworthiness of an aircraft?
questions.explanation: While mechanics perform inspections and repairs, ultimate responsibility for maintaining an aircraft's airworthiness rests with its owner or operator.

questions.question: Who must conduct an annual inspection?
options: A. An A&P technician holding Inspection Authorization (IA)
C. Any A&P technician, without IA
questions.explanation: The annual inspection specifically requires a mechanic who holds both an A&P certificate and Inspection Authorization, distinguishing it from the 100-hour inspection requirement.

questions.question: Which aviation regulation part specifies inspection requirements referenced for large aircraft or multiengine operations in this context?
questions.explanation: General operating and flight rules, including various inspection program requirements applicable to different aircraft categories including large/multiengine aircraft, are found under 14 CFR Part 91.

questions.question: Which inspection phase includes completing the work order?
options: C. The return to service phase
questions.explanation: The pre-inspection phase involves administrative preparation, including completing the work order and gathering necessary documentation before the physical inspection begins.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of inspection process steps?
options: B. Look, service and repair, functional test
questions.explanation: A logical inspection sequence begins with visually assessing (looking at) the aircraft's condition, followed by any needed servicing/repair, and concluding with functional testing to confirm proper operation.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of these inspection phases: repair, functional test, and return to service?
options: A. Repair, functional test, return to service (in that order)
B. Functional test, repair, return to service
C. Return to service, repair, functional test
questions.explanation: After identifying and completing necessary repairs, a functional test verifies proper operation before the aircraft is formally approved and returned to service.

questions.question: Which inspection phase consists of preparing the maintenance record, gathering tools, and similar preparatory tasks?
questions.explanation: The pre-inspection phase covers administrative and logistical preparation—paperwork, tool staging, and planning—before the hands-on inspection work begins.

questions.question: What type of inspection breaks the annual inspection into segments accomplished over time, in order to reduce aircraft downtime?
questions.explanation: Progressive inspection programs divide the comprehensive annual-equivalent inspection into smaller, scheduled segments, reducing the amount of time the aircraft is out of service at once.

questions.question: During a 100-hour inspection, if a defect is found, what must the person disapproving the aircraft for return to service do?
options: A. Report/record the reason for disapproval in the maintenance record
B. Simply ground the aircraft with no documentation
C. Repair the defect themselves regardless of certification
questions.explanation: The inspector disapproving return to service must document the specific reason(s) for disapproval in the maintenance record, giving the owner/operator clear information on what must be corrected.

questions.question: How often is an annual inspection required?
questions.explanation: Federal aviation regulations require most aircraft to undergo an annual inspection at intervals not exceeding 12 calendar months.

questions.question: A progressive inspection program must be completed within what time period?
questions.explanation: A progressive inspection program's segmented tasks must collectively cover the full inspection scope and be completed within a 12-month cycle.

questions.question: Before an aircraft can be returned to service, what must be done to determine whether a system operates within limits?
options: A. A weight and balance recalculation
questions.explanation: A functional check verifies that a repaired or inspected system actually operates correctly and within its specified limits before the aircraft is returned to service.

questions.question: What ensures that an aircraft is properly inspected with no items overlooked?
options: C. A work order number alone
questions.explanation: Using a detailed checklist during inspection helps ensure every required item is systematically checked, reducing the risk of something being missed.

questions.question: In magnetic particle inspection, which type of magnetization is used to detect a defect running circumferentially around a cylinder?
questions.explanation: To detect circumferential (around-the-cylinder) defects, the magnetic field must run longitudinally (along the length) of the part, since defects show up best when oriented across the magnetic flux lines.

questions.question: In magnetic particle inspection, which type of magnetization is used to detect a longitudinal defect running along a cylinder?
questions.explanation: To detect defects running lengthwise along a cylinder, circular magnetization (field running around the circumference) is used, since the defect must lie across the magnetic flux lines to be detected.

questions.question: What are Engineering Orders (EO)?
options: A. Official paperwork issued by engineering, approved by QA, and usually implemented through the Production Planning and Control (PP&C) organization
B. Informal notes made by a mechanic with no approval needed
C. Pilot reports logged after each flight
questions.explanation: Engineering Orders are formal, QA-approved engineering documents that direct specific maintenance/modification actions, typically routed through production planning and control for implementation.

questions.question: After maintenance and/or inspection, and before an aircraft can be returned to service, what should the technician conduct?
questions.explanation: Before returning an aircraft to service, the technician should conduct operational checks to confirm that repaired or inspected systems function correctly.

questions.question: What is a primary function of Technical Publications within an organization?
options: A. To establish and maintain a complete, up-to-date library system for all documents needed for Maintenance & Engineering (M&E) operations
B. To design new aircraft structures
questions.explanation: The Technical Publications function ensures that current, accurate maintenance documentation (manuals, bulletins, ADs) is maintained and readily accessible to support maintenance and engineering operations.

questions.question: Each time a life-limited part is removed from a type-certificated product, what must happen to its tag or record?
options: A. No documentation update is required
B. A new tag/record must be created, or the existing tag/record must be updated with the current life status
C. The part's history can simply be discarded
questions.explanation: Life-limited parts require continuous tracking, so removal triggers either creation of a new tag/record or an update to the existing one reflecting accumulated life/cycles.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about temporary maintenance records?
options: A. That they are kept by the owner until the recorded work is repeated or superseded
B. That they may be discarded after 1 year has elapsed since the work was performed
C. That they are not recorded at all
questions.explanation: Temporary records absolutely are recorded and retained (at least until superseded or a defined time period passes); claiming they are "not recorded at all" is false.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way that aircraft documentation digital data can be made available?
options: A. Hardcopy format (hardcopy is physical, not digital, data)
C. Server access or the Internet
questions.explanation: Hardcopy (printed paper) format is a physical medium, not a digital data delivery method, distinguishing it from CD/DVD or server/internet-based digital access.

questions.question: A preflight inspection is a required inspection to determine the condition of the aircraft for the flight to be conducted, and is the responsibility of whom?
questions.explanation: Regulations place responsibility for the preflight inspection and determination of the aircraft's airworthiness for that flight on the pilot-in-command.

questions.question: An entire progressive inspection must be completed within how many calendar months?
questions.explanation: Like the annual inspection it replaces in segmented form, a progressive inspection program's full cycle must be completed within 12 calendar months.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding inspection substitution?
options: A. An annual inspection is valid in place of a 100-hour inspection
B. A 100-hour inspection is valid in place of an annual inspection
C. A daily inspection is valid in place of a 100-hour inspection
questions.explanation: Because the annual inspection requirement is more stringent (requiring IA certification), completing it satisfies the 100-hour inspection requirement as well.

questions.question: The task cards produced by the airframe manufacturer are usually designed for what purpose?
options: A. One action only (a single discrete task per card)
B. Multiple unrelated tasks combined on one card
C. General reference only, with no specific task
questions.explanation: Manufacturer task cards are typically structured to document one specific maintenance action per card, keeping each task clearly defined and traceable.

questions.question: What is a logbook used to record?
options: A. Only the pilot's flight hours
C. The time in service, maintenance, alterations, inspections, and AD compliance for the airframe and its associated components/appliances
questions.explanation: Aircraft logbooks serve as the historical record of time in service, all maintenance actions, alterations, inspections performed, and compliance with Airworthiness Directives.

questions.question: If a major repair or major alteration is performed on an aircraft, how must it be returned to service?
options: A. By a simple logbook entry with no specific form
B. By a verbal statement to the FAA only
C. By use of an FAA Form 337
questions.explanation: Major repairs and alterations require documentation on FAA Form 337 (Major Repair and Alteration form) as part of properly returning the aircraft to service.

questions.question: What type of inspection is performed on aircraft operated for flight instruction or hire that is not itself FAA-mandated by that specific name?
questions.explanation: Similar to the 50-hour interim check concept, some operators schedule a non-mandatory interim inspection (such as a 40-hour check) between required inspections, as an added precaution for hard-used training aircraft.

questions.question: What sources can outside documents used in aircraft maintenance come from?
options: B. Only the original aircraft purchaser
C. Airframe and engine manufacturers, vendors/manufacturers of installed equipment, and the owner
questions.explanation: Maintenance-relevant documentation comes from multiple outside sources, including airframe/engine OEMs, equipment vendors, and information supplied by the aircraft owner.

questions.question: Which of the following is a comprehensive and complete inspection that can be performed by a certificated A&P mechanic?
options: C. The progressive inspection authorization review
questions.explanation: The 100-hour inspection, while comprehensive, can be signed off by a standard A&P mechanic, unlike the annual inspection which requires Inspection Authorization.

questions.question: Which inspection is detailed to the same scope/content as an annual inspection?
questions.explanation: A 100-hour inspection uses the same scope and checklist items (per FAR 43 Appendix D) as an annual inspection; the key difference is who is authorized to perform/sign it off.

questions.question: A basic preflight inspection and walk-around is also known as what?
questions.explanation: The routine check performed before the first flight each day, including a walk-around, is commonly termed a Daily Inspection.

questions.question: When does the pre-inspection phase begin?
options: A. When the aircraft engine is started for a test flight
B. When the owner of the aircraft requests the service of a shop to perform an inspection, including completing a work order and documentation
C. Only after the inspection has been fully completed
questions.explanation: The pre-inspection phase starts at the point the owner initiates the inspection request, kicking off administrative steps like work order creation before any physical work begins.

questions.question: What does the documentation abbreviation "AC" stand for?
questions.explanation: In the context of FAA documentation, "AC" commonly refers to Advisory Circulars, which provide guidance material on various aviation topics.
